description:
The JSON storage backend applies a redo record to the filesystem and re-applies a leftover one idempotently, stepping through named interruption points.

## Background

Applying a record replaces each put path by temp-file and rename, removes each deleted path, writes the event append at its recorded offset, and removes the record. Re-application is the same code: a put overwrites, a delete tolerates an absent target, and the append rewrites the same bytes at the same offset, so a record applied twice converges on the same state. Parent directories are created as a put needs them, because both backends verify parents and a delta omitting ancestors fails apply.

The positioned append holds three conditions. The offset is the captured file length rather than a line boundary, because the event composer may begin the appended bytes with a separator newline and the torn-tail protocol admits an incomplete final line. The file is opened without append mode, since append mode ignores the offset and would double-append. Re-application truncates to the offset plus the appended length, so a longer file converges.

Interruption points make the mechanism's crash matrix testable at unit cost. They are a closed enum over the steps of apply and re-application, reached through an injector the backend holds, in the shape the storage layer already uses.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Applying a record to a data root replaces each put path, removes each delete path, writes the append at its offset, and removes the record.
- [hard] REQ-02: A put whose parent directories are absent creates them before the replacement.
- [hard] REQ-03: Re-applying a record over a state where some operations already landed produces the same final bytes as a single clean application, for any prefix of the operation order.
- [hard] REQ-04: The event append is written without append mode at the recorded offset, and the file is truncated to the offset plus the appended length.
- [hard] REQ-05: A closed interruption-point enum names each step of apply and re-application, and the backend checks every point through an injector it holds.
- [hard] REQ-06: A record naming a path outside the data root and the worktree is refused before any live write.
- [hard] REQ-07: The apply module is declared beside the storage layer's other public backends, so the workspace builds with no warnings while nothing calls it.

## Notes

Expected additive footprint is under 350 production lines. The interruption points name the steps of this mechanism alone.
title: File-backend record application
